Question:
In the diagram below, a diameter of each of the two smaller circles is a radius of the larger circle. If the two smaller circles have a combined area of \(1\) square unit, then what is the area of the shaded region, in square units?

[Figure 1](figures/2018_AMC_8_Q15_question_fig1.svg)
Solution:
The two smaller circles have the same radius, because each diameter equals a radius of the large circle. Call their common radius \(r\). The large circle then has radius \(2r\), so its area is \(\pi(2r)^2=4\pi r^2\).

The two small circles together have area \(2\pi r^2=1\). The large circle therefore has twice that combined area, or \(2\) square units. Removing the two small white circles leaves shaded area

\[
2-1=\boxed{1}\text{ square unit},
\]

choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\). Doubling a radius multiplies area by four.
